pr_title: Delay searchable snapshot allocation during shutdown
pr_body:
During a shutdown, searchable snapshots should not be re-allocated to new nodes,
since this leads to data download. Instead, now wait for the shutdown reallocation
delay before reallocating shards.

Fixes #85052
pr_comments: Hi @henningandersen, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> This looks good but I suspect that the test will cause failures on CI

Thanks for capturing this and also for figuring out that this happens when a shard receives no data. I amended the test to create multiple indices with one shard, seemed like the easiest route to guarantee docs in every shard. Ready or another look.

issue_context.title: Shards are relocated while node is restarted and shutdown API has been called
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

7.17.1

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

ECK running on GKE 1.22.7-gke.900

### Problem Description

Shards are relocated between nodes in the cold tier while they are restarting, despite the fact that the [shutdown API](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/put-shutdown.html#put-shutdown-api-request-body) is called with the type `restart`.

It has been first reported by an ECK user [here](https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/issues/5464):
> I see the managed Elasticsearch cluster try to reallocate 350+ searchable snapshots from the restart of a cold node.

I also managed to reproduce it consistently:

1. See a first report [here](https://gist.github.com/barkbay/ef1c7b516bf93534d216bfa48827b70d), full logs from the master node are [here](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/barkbay/0f25a9588755a8eb06bea0a70ec6a1a7/raw/bfe10bf910ac2ae0ffab07454395fd4d694e0cc1/master-0.ndjson).

2. I also reproduced the problem while `logger.org.elasticsearch.cluster.routing.allocation.decider` was set to true `TRACE`,  logs are available [here](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/barkbay/0f25a9588755a8eb06bea0a70ec6a1a7/raw/bfe10bf910ac2ae0ffab07454395fd4d694e0cc1/master-0.traces.ndjson). While the node `elasticsearch-gcs-sample-es-cold-2` is restarted, shard `restored-.ds-metricbeat-8.0.0-2022.03.16-000003` has been relocated to `elasticsearch-gcs-sample-es-cold-1`.


It does not seem to happen for other tiers (not sure about the frozen though).


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy a cluster with a cold tier, shards being backed by a snapshot. Without replica.
2. Call the shutdown API with the `restart` type on a node in the cold tier
3. Monitor the shards location
4. Restart the node
5. Shards are being relocated


### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_
comments: Had a look at this and it looks like the `SearchableSnapshotEnableAllocationDecider` needs to also look for a shutdown indication or another mechanism need to ensure that these searchable snapshot shards are not reallocated within the `allocation_delay` period. Notice that these are primaries, which is why the mechanism for replicas does not kick in.

In case anyone comes across this issue before it is fixed, and they don't want their searchable snapshot shards reallocating during a rolling restart. The following hacky script can be run before performing a rolling restart, and should negate searchable snapshots from being reallocated.

# Note

This solution primarily refers to a case where you don't have control over the rolling restart process (like ECK), where the normal solution:

```json
PUT _cluster/settings
{
  "persistent": {
    "cluster.routing.allocation.enable": "primaries"
  }
}
```

Doesn't really work, as trying to time when ECK will start restarting the next node is challenging.

## Prerequisites 
- bash
- jq
- curl

## Variables

- `ES_USERNAME` username of the user that has the ability to set index settings
- `ES_PASSWORD` password of the user you're using
- `ES_URL` URL to your Elasticsearch cluster

## Assumptions
1. This script assumes the searchable snapshot indices are managed by ILM and start with the prefix `restored-*`. If your searchable snapshots aren't managed by ILM or don't begin with the `restored-*` prefix. Change the script to use which ever pattern(s) work for you.
2. The script assumes that a single shard is backing each index.
3. Only `open` & `hidden` indices are considered, if you also have closed searchable snapshots change `expand_wildcards=open,hidden` to `expand_wildcards=all`
4. Some `timeout` values are set as some operations might take a bit and its just easier to increase the timeout than trying to add retry logic. Adjust as needed.

## Script

**Updated 2022-04-22:** Updated the script with an `if` condition to ignore indices that are in the middle of being transferred (reallocated) to a new node (ignore node names (`${node_name1}`) that contain `->`)

Run this (and wait till finished) before performing a rolling restart.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
echo $(curl -k -X GET "https://${ES_USERNAME}:${ES_PASSWORD}@${ES_URL}:9200/_cat/indices/restored-*?h=i,id,n&v&expand_wildcards=open,hidden&format=json") | jq -rc '.[] ' | while read row; do
        echo "--------------------Start---------------------------------"
        index_name=$(echo "${row}" | jq -r '.i')
        echo "Index Name/Id: ${index_name}"
        echo ""
        echo "Get Shard Data:"
        echo $(curl -k -X GET "https://${ES_USERNAME}:${ES_PASSWORD}@${ES_URL}:9200/_cat/shards/${index_name}?h=i,id,n&format=json")  | jq -rc '.[] ' | while read row1; do
        echo ""
        echo "Shard Data:"
        echo "${row1}"
        index_name1=$(echo "${row1}" | jq -r '.i')
        node_id1=$(echo "${row1}" | jq -r '.id')
        node_name1=$(echo "${row1}" | jq -r '.n')
        echo ""
        echo "Index Name/Id: ${index_name1}"
        echo ""
        echo "Node Id: ${node_id1}"
        echo ""
        echo "Node Name: ${node_name1}"
        echo ""
        if grep -vq "\->" <<< "${node_name1}"; then
                echo "Curl Index-level Shard Command"
                curl_command=$(curl -k -X PUT "https://${ES_USERNAME}:${ES_PASSWORD}@${ES_URL}:9200/${index_name1}/_settings?timeout=120s" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"index.routing.allocation.require._name\": \"${node_name1}\"}")
                echo ""
                echo "Curl Command Output"
                echo ""
                echo "${curl_command}"
        else
                echo "Bad Node Name"
        fi
        done
        echo "---------------------End---------------------------------"
done
```

## Explanation

1. Get a list of all indices that match our pattern (`restored-*`) (including hidden) via `_cat/indices`.
5. Loop through this list
    1. Get the shard information of the index via `_cat/shards`
        1. **Note:** Can't use `_cat/shards` initially because of: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/84656 where `restored-*` doesn't expand `hidden` indices/shards
    2. Get the index name (`index_name1`), node id (`node_id1`), and node name (`node_name1`) of the shard.
        1. **Note:** The script only really uses index name (`index_name1`) and node name (`node_name1`), but include the node id (`node_id1`) for debugging/troubleshooting.
    4. Update the shard's index settings to lock `index.routing.allocation.require._name` to its current node name (`node_name1`)
        1. This locks the shard/index to its current node, therefore when the node restarts, Elasticsearch won't attempt reallocate it.

## Cleanup

After the rolling upgrade is complete, to be able to allow for allocations to go back to normal, `null` out the routing allocation change:

```bash
curl -k -X PUT "https://${ES_USERNAME}:${ES_PASSWORD}@${ES_URL}:9200/restored-*/_settings?timeout=120s&expand_wildcards=open,hidden" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"index.routing.allocation.require._name\": null}"
```
@henningandersen I've reassigned to distributed as you all have the expertise to update `SearchableSnapshotEnableAllocationDecider` to be shutdown aware.

review_comments: I wonder if this can cause some test failures when a low number of data nodes is picked up? I quickly tested with a 10 shards index and 2 data nodes and got a failure after ~5 runs.
